title: Take-rate & HC Hedgebook: committed vs burst phasing (Q2 2026)
content:
Executive summary:
This workbook articulates a hedging approach that couples take-rate assumptions (customer adoption of paid tiers) with headcount phasing and contracting levers (committed slabs, microcommitments, burst credits). Objective: protect runway while preserving go-to-market velocity for high-potential deals.

Key point: small shifts in enterprise take-rate (±3 percentage points) materially change committed capacity needs and therefore near-term HC requirements for SRE/Serving Ops. This hedgebook defines trigger thresholds, an HC ramp/backfill timeline, and pricing experiments to soften runaway hires.

Assumptions (base case):
- ARR bucket: mid-market + enterprise pipeline coverage estimated at $26M ARR ARR-equivalent demand for FY27.
- Current take-rate (free->paid conversion on product): 6.8% (weighted by segment).
- Conversion sensitivity window tested: 4.5% — 9.5%.
- Throughput per dedicated GPU pool: baseline 120k tokens/min (on typical RLHF-style workloads).
- Cost per committed GPU-month (weighted avg): $3,900 (includes infra, amortized infra ops).
- Average monthly token consumption per paying customer: 1.2M tokens.

Baseline headcount mapping (directly supporting inference capacity):
- 0–$10M ARR: 2 serving-engineers, 1 infra-sre, 1 onboarding PM
- $10–$30M ARR: +3 serving-engineers, +2 infra-sre, +1 solutions SE
- $30M+: +5 serving-engineers per additional $20M ARR (scale step)

Scenario matrix (summary lines):
- Upside (take-rate +3pp): aggressive self-serve monetization succeeds -> need for earlier committed pools and +4 FTE (serving) in Q3 to meet latency SLOs for paid traffic.
- Base: current plan, keep 2 committed pools, stagger hiring across Q3–Q4.
- Downside (take-rate -2pp): slower conversion; postpone committed purchases, rely on burst credits and temporary contractors; net HC add = +1 (onboarding) only.

Pseudo-sheet: headcount phasing table (quarters)
Quarter | Trigger metric | Hiring action | Role | Notes
Q2 2026 | pipeline-conversion > 7.5% for 4w | Start recruiting | 2 Sr. Serving Eng | stagger offers, start in Q3
Q3 2026 | committed-contract signed (>= $500k) | Reserve capacity + hire | 3 Serving Eng, 1 Infra-SRE | prioritize SLO-critical infra
Q3 2026 | sustained paid traffic > 1.5x baseline | Fast-fail hiring | 2 Solutions SE (contract->perm) | use microcommitment credits in interim
Q4 2026 | take-rate dips below 5% | Hiring freeze + contractors | 0 perm; 2 contractors | pull offers if not accepted by deadline

Pricing sensitivity (selected experiments):
- Microcommitments (30–90 day): price premium 5–8% vs monthly; expected to raise committed revenue share by +1.2pp with low sales friction.
- Slab discounting: 6-month slab with 10% discount increases conversion on trials by estimated +2.1pp for mid-market.
- Burst-credit bundles: sell burst credits at 1.5x spot price; expected uptake by 12% of customers; reduces immediate committed GPU buys.

Quantitative outputs (high-level):
- If take-rate moves from 6.8% -> 9.8%: projected committed GPU-months required rise +48%, incremental monthly cost ~$180k; requires +4 FTE serving ops to preserve 99th percentile latency.
- If take-rate falls to 4.8%: committed GPU demand drops -35%; runway extends by ~2.1 months at current burn (assuming hiring pauses and slab deferments).

Trigger rules (operational):
- Pipeline-to-conversion delta: if 4-week rolling conversion > +1.5pp vs plan -> open 60% of planned reqs for serving engineering (candidate pipeline share)
- Contract velocity: >= 2 enterprise slabs >= $250k in 30 days -> lock 1 committed GPU pool + move 40% of planned hires to Q3
- Cost trigger: marginal unit-cost (per-1M tokens) > baseline by 12% -> pause slabs and shift to burst credits + instant quantization rollout (ops playbook)

Recommended playbook (short):
1) Implement a 30/60/90 visibility dashboard for conversion, paid-token growth, and committed-contract pipeline. Owners: Ops Finance + Growth.
2) Pilot microcommitment product with 5 strategic mid-market customers (offer limited-time slab stacking) — sales + legal to draft template.
3) Prepare a 6-week contractor bench (three vetted infra contractors) to avoid immediate perm hires in the downside scenario.
4) Pre-authorize one deferred offer tranche for serving-engineering (60% of candidate comp deferred) to preserve speed while reducing near-term burn.

Open questions / risks:
- Sales cycle sensitivity: will mid-market accept microcommitments? Risk: adoption might cannibalize full-term committed revenue.
- Capacity-lag: procurement lead time for dedicated hardware vs CPU inference fallbacks.
- Talent market: candidate supply for specialized serving engineers may slow on 6–8 week timeline.

Appendix: quick calculation snapshot
- Baseline paying customers estimate: 3,450 (weighted mix)
- Avg tokens/month/customer: 1.2M -> baseline token demand = ~4.14B tokens/month
- GPU-months baseline (committed) estimate: 72 -> cost @ $3,900 = $280.8k/mo
- Upside (+3pp take-rate) GPU-months estimate: 107 -> incremental cost = $104.1k/mo

Next steps (this doc):
- Finance: bake the hedgebook into Q3 budget cadence and publish a scenario summary by June 15.
- GTM/sales: confirm 5 pilot accounts for microcommitment by June 30.
- Eng leadership: validate contractor bench and a 6-week ramp plan; provide ops playbook for quantization rollout by June 20.

Notes to reviewer: this is intentionally operation-focused (short-term HC levers tied to pricing experiments). The goal is to create flexible hiring posture that reacts to leading indicators (conversion & contract velocity) rather than lagging revenue. Please add lane-specific constraints (legal, procurement) below when you review.
